Important: clearing one scanner warning clears that signal only. It does not prove the whole control passes.

text:
Timing: 2:00
Keep this high-level. The trigger is what the application does and whose data or decisions it affects.
GDPR requires data protection by design/default. EU online-selling guidance lists advance information duties. The European Accessibility Act covers e-commerce among other services.
As checked on 11 August 2026, the AI Act is generally applicable, with specific transition dates for some high-risk systems. Verify the current scope and national implementation for the use case.
Use OWASP Top 10 for awareness, OWASP ASVS 5.0 for testable security requirements and WCAG 2.2 as a practical accessibility target.
This slide is general education, not legal advice.

[Sources]
- https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/information-business-and-organisations/obligations/what-does-data-protection-design-and-default-mean_en

- https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/policies/justice-and-fundamental-rights/disability/european-accessibility-act-eaa_en
- https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai

[/Sources]

name: slide-8-title
text: The ten-question launch check
textPreview: The ten-question launch check

name: slide-8-question-1
text: Can someone explain the app and data flow in five sentences?
textPreview: Can someone explain the app and data flow in five sentences?

name: slide-8-question-2
text: Does the business own the domain, repository, database and accounts?
textPreview: Does the business own the domain, repository, database and accounts?

name: slide-8-question-3
text: Were secrets checked in current code and Git history?
textPreview: Were secrets checked in current code and Git history?

name: slide-8-question-4
text: Was access tested with two different user accounts?
textPreview: Was access tested with two different user accounts?

name: slide-8-question-5
text: Are permissions enforced by the backend or database?
textPreview: Are permissions enforced by the backend or database?

name: slide-8-question-6
text: Are inputs validated, queries safe and uploads limited?
textPreview: Are inputs validated, queries safe and uploads limited?

name: slide-8-question-7
text: Are payments and webhooks signed and duplicate-safe?
textPreview: Are payments and webhooks signed and duplicate-safe?

name: slide-8-question-8
text: Are expensive actions authenticated, limited and budget-capped?
textPreview: Are expensive actions authenticated, limited and budget-capped?

name: slide-8-question-9
text: Were the main journey, alerts and backup restore actually tested?
textPreview: Were the main journey, alerts and backup restore actually tested?

name: slide-8-question-10
text: Is there evidence for applicable privacy, consumer, accessibility and AI duties?
textPreview: Is there evidence for applicable privacy, consumer, accessibility and AI duties?

name: slide-8-callout
text: Critical or High risk is not a Pass without evidence.
textPreview: Critical or High risk is not a Pass without evidence.

text:
Timing: 3:00
Invite the audience to photograph this slide or use it as the take-home handout.
A checklist reduces risk; it does not certify an application as secure.
For each answer, request evidence: a test result, configuration, screenshot, log, restore record or named owner and due date.

name: slide-9-final-question
text:
Do not ask, “Does it look finished?”
Ask, “What evidence says it behaves safely?”
textPreview: Do not ask, “Does it look finished?” | Ask, “What evidence says it behaves safely?”

text:
Timing: 1:15
Close with three actions: test the access boundary with two accounts; run dedicated secret and dependency scanners; give every unanswered item an owner and due date.
Final message: vibe coding makes software faster to create—not safer to publish. A good review replaces confidence with evidence.
